record.question:
A company runs an increasing number of ECS tasks on Fargate On-Demand in one AWS account and Region. Task sizes vary. Operations needs an SNS notification when concurrently running Fargate vCPUs exceed 75% of the applicable quota. The team wants to avoid custom metric publishers and manual updates when the quota changes.

Which solution is the most operationally efficient?

options.text: Use the SampleCount statistic for ECS CPUUtilization as the number of running vCPUs. Divide it by the Fargate quota and create a CloudWatch alarm.
Select the AWS/Usage ResourceCount metric with Service=Fargate, Type=Resource, Resource=vCPU, and Class=Standard/OnDemand. Alarm on 100*m1/SERVICE_QUOTA(m1) greater than 75 and notify an SNS topic.
Request a larger Fargate quota and configure an AWS Health event rule to publish an SNS notification whenever consumption reaches 75% of the new quota.
Publish a custom count of running ECS tasks, divide it by a manually configured task limit, and alarm when that percentage exceeds 75.

explanation.text:
Correct: <<2>>. Fargate publishes account usage as ResourceCount in AWS/Usage. The dimensions select On-Demand vCPU consumption, and SERVICE_QUOTA returns the associated quota for the usage metric. A metric-math alarm can notify SNS without maintaining a separate publisher or hard-coded quota value.

<<1>> is incorrect because SampleCount counts samples included in a metric statistic; it is not the number of allocated vCPUs. CPUUtilization also measures utilization rather than quota consumption.

<<3>> changes the ceiling but does not create the requested usage-threshold monitor. AWS Health is not a replacement for this CloudWatch usage alarm.

<<4>> uses task count, which diverges from vCPU usage when task sizes differ, and adds custom maintenance.

Match the metric dimensions and quota scope. Fargate Spot uses a separate class and quota, so monitor it separately if introduced. Set the alarm period and evaluation policy deliberately; crossing 75% does not guarantee enough capacity remains until someone responds.

Official AWS references (checked 2026-09-18):
[Fargate usage metrics](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonECS/latest/developerguide/monitoring-fargate-usage.html)
[CloudWatch quota alarms](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/monitoring/CloudWatch-Quotas-Visualize-Alarms.html)

diagram_alt: A numerical example shows why allocated vCPU usage divided by its matching quota determines the alarm.

sources.supports: ResourceCount dimensions distinguish vCPU usage and On-Demand versus Spot
SERVICE_QUOTA expression supports percentage-based usage alarms

editorial_notes: Removed irrelevant ECS Anywhere plans, specified On-Demand/account/Region scope and variable task sizes, and corrected the original explanation of SampleCount. Answer unchanged.
